name: Improper Input Validation
remediation: Validate type, length, range, and format at the trust boundary.

name: Path Traversal
remediation: Use canonical paths and restrict access to an intended directory.

name: Command Injection
remediation: Avoid shells and use fixed argument arrays with allowlisted commands.

name: OS Command Injection
remediation: Do not pass untrusted input to operating-system commands.

name: Cross-site Scripting
remediation: Encode by output context and sanitize supported rich text.

name: SQL Injection
remediation: Use bound parameters and ORM query composition.

name: LDAP Injection
remediation: Escape LDAP filter and distinguished-name contexts independently.

name: XML Injection
remediation: Use safe XML generation and strict schema validation.

name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
remediation: Apply the correct encoder for each output context.

name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
remediation: Normalize control characters and avoid sensitive log content.

name: Exposure of Sensitive Information
remediation: Minimize returned data and enforce need-to-know authorization.

name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
remediation: Return generic errors and keep diagnostics in protected logs.

name: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges
remediation: Drop capabilities and run with the least required privilege.

name: Use of Hard-coded Password
remediation: Use a secret manager and rotate exposed credentials.

name: Improper Access Control
remediation: Enforce deny-by-default authorization on every protected operation.

name: Improper Authentication
remediation: Use resistant MFA and verify every session on the server.

name: Improper Certificate Validation
remediation: Validate chains, hostnames, expiry, and revocation policy.

name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
remediation: Require authenticated, authorized sessions for critical functions.

name: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
remediation: Encrypt sensitive data with managed keys and authenticated encryption.

name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
remediation: Require modern TLS on every network hop carrying sensitive data.

name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
remediation: Use current approved algorithms, key sizes, and rotation.

name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
remediation: Migrate to maintained authenticated-encryption constructions.

name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
remediation: Use SameSite cookies and validated anti-CSRF tokens where cookies authenticate.

name: Session Fixation
remediation: Rotate session identifiers after authentication and privilege changes.

name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
remediation: Set concurrency, memory, CPU, input-size, and execution-time limits.

name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
remediation: Use simple signed data formats and never instantiate arbitrary types.

name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
remediation: Disable DTDs and external entities and use defused parsers.

name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
remediation: Derive tenant access on the server instead of trusting object identifiers.

name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
remediation: Restrict filesystem and object-store permissions to required principals.

name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
remediation: Remove embedded credentials and automate managed secret rotation.

name: Missing Authorization
remediation: Authorize every action and object on the server.

name: Incorrect Authorization
remediation: Test role, assignment, scope, and tenant rules independently.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery
remediation: Allowlist outbound destinations and enforce network-level egress controls.
